messages.subject: Help with hierarchical negative binomial
parts:
Hi all,

I have been trying to run this negative binomial regression model, but something is wrong and I can't figure out what. I think it might be obvious. Here is my model:

hmod = '

data {

int<lower=0> numL; // num of locations

int<lower=0> numN; // total num of non-indep data

real x[numL]; // x n

int<lower=1> y[numN]; // y n

int<lower=1, upper=numL> loc[numN]; // location ID

}

parameters {

real b1;

real b2;

real b3;

real<lower=0> p1; // p parameter of negative binomial

real<lower=0, upper=10> sigma; // variance between the means

// parameters for each location

real<lower=0> mu_y[numL]; // mean Y for each location

}

model {

// Priors

b1 ~ normal(0, 10);

b2 ~ normal(0, 10);

b3 ~ normal(0, 10);

p1 ~ cauchy(0, 5);

sigma ~ uniform(0, 10);

// likelihood

for (n in 1:numN) {

y[n] ~ neg_binomial(exp(mu_y[loc[n]]), p1);

}

for (i in 1:numL) {

mu_y[i] ~ normal((b1 / (1 + exp(b2 + b3 * x[i]))), sigma);

}

}

'

Here are some random data that reflect my current data

dat = list(numL = 10, numN = 100, y = rnegbin(100, 8, 9), x = rep(rnorm(10), 10), loc = rep(1:10, 10))


But when I try to run the model

smod = stan(model_code = hmod, data = dat, chains = 0)


I get the following error:

TRANSLATING MODEL 'hmod' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'hmod' with error message:
EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=input; line=35, column=1

Parser expecting: <model declaration>

messages.author: 484c91357ac83f6b
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Help with hierarchical negative binomial
parts:
I don't know what's causing the compile error. But, one thing I saw on your model specification: you seem to be assuming that neg_binomial from Stan uses the parametrization of GLMs, that is, negBinomial(mean, overdispersion). But Stan doesn't, it uses a parametrization of Bayesian Data Analysis book, see the Stan manual.

R doesn't use it neither, it uses the simple parametrization that is taught in introductory undergraduate probability courses (see Wikipedia). To use the parametrization negBinomial(mean, overdispersion) in R, you must do:
rnbinom(100, 8, mu=9), where 100 is the number of draws to be generated, 8 is the overdispersion parameter and 9 is the mean.
